last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarter ever, with adjusted earnings of $2.85 a share, up 22%, helped by a jump in investment gains and growth in every segment.

takeaways.label: Record, investment-aided profit
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share rose 22% to $2.85 excluding one-time items. Profit from volatile investments (private equity and similar) jumped 49% to $720 million, so part of the strength may not repeat.

takeaways.label: Growth everywhere
takeaways.text: Premiums, fees and other revenue rose 12% to $14.1 billion, or 8% excluding large pension deals. All six business segments grew, and Europe, Middle East and Africa earnings rose 24%.

takeaways.label: Returns and cash flow
takeaways.text: Adjusted return on equity was 19.6% excluding one-time items, up from 16.7% a year earlier. MetLife returned about $1 billion to shareholders and says it is on track for its full-year cash-flow and expense targets.

takeaways.label: Soft spots
takeaways.text: Asia sales fell 6% against a strong year-earlier quarter. Retirement and Income Solutions earnings fell 6% after an annual insurance-assumptions review, though they rose 12% excluding that charge.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
